statement: aud-uncertainty-child-register illustrates plain child-facing uncertainty with polite -요 forms ('아직 확실하지 않아요', '그럴 수도 있어요'), while the SUE-570 child baselines are written throughout in casual 반말 ('~야', '~아'). The Writer kept 반말 for internal consistency and flagged the ambiguity rather than switching register mid-document, which was the right call. But the pack does not say anywhere which politeness level a child-facing Korean piece should use, and Korean has no neutral option — every sentence ending commits to one. The rule's examples therefore read as if they mandate -요 when they are only illustrating plainness. This is a genuine hole rather than a misreading: an agent following the pack literally would produce a register clash the pack never warned about. Recorded at task_local scope: this is an agent observation, and basis "model_inference" may not carry scope "calibration_candidate" on its own — agent consensus never silently becomes durable preference. Promoting this finding into the pack requires the owner.

routing.rationale: Politeness level in Korean child-facing writing is an audience-constraint question — it is about the relationship the text assumes with its reader — and the shared audience layer owns 'depth, jargon tolerance, purpose framing'. Not owner_voice: nobody has expressed a preference, and treating an unspecified default as taste would invent owner preference from silence. Not normative: both 반말 and -요 are correct Korean, so no standards body decides this.
